name: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Ziyād ibn al-Aʿrābī
summary: Kufan lexicographer of great memory, the stepson and student of al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī, and teacher of Thaʿlab and Ibn al-Sikkīt.
bio: Ibn al-Aʿrābī was born in Kufa in 150/767, the son of a slave from Sind, and grew up in the house of the anthologist al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī, his stepfather, with whom and with al-Kisāʾī he studied. Al-Zubaydī places him in the second generation of the Kufan lexicographers.

He taught from memory and is said never to have been seen with a book; Thaʿlab, who studied with him for years, said he had never seen anyone know more rare words. His Kitāb al-Nawādir is known through quotations. He died in Samarra in 231/846.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 120 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
